question: What corpus was HelixNet trained on?
reference_answer: HelixNet was pre-trained and fine-tuned on the TerraNotes corpus of 1.2 million de-identified clinical notes.

evidence.quote: HelixNet was pre-trained and fine-tuned on the TerraNotes corpus

question: By how many F1 points did HelixNet beat ClinBERT-L on diagnosis coding?
reference_answer: By 4.2 F1 points (71.8 versus 67.6 micro-averaged F1).

evidence.quote: HelixNet reaches a micro-averaged F1 score of 71.8, compared with 67.6 for ClinBERT-L, an improvement of 4.2 F1 points

question: How large is the local attention window in HelixNet, and how many global tokens does it use?
reference_answer: A local window of 512 tokens plus 32 global summary tokens.

evidence.quote: each token attends to a local window of 512 tokens plus a small set of 32 global summary tokens

question: Under what licence is the TerraNotes corpus released?
reference_answer: For research use only, under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 (CC BY-NC 4.0); commercial use is not permitted.

evidence.quote: released for research use only under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 licence (CC BY-NC 4.0)

question: How much did the coding tool reduce coding time at St. Aurelia Hospital?
reference_answer: By 31 percent, from 13 minutes to 9 minutes per discharge summary.

evidence.quote: the average time a coder spent on one discharge summary fell by 31 percent, from 13 minutes to 9 minutes

question: What was WindowFormer's peak inference memory on a 9,000-token note?

evidence.quote: 14.3 GB for WindowFormer

question: How was de-identification of TerraNotes checked?
reference_answer: A rule-based tool removed identifiers, then a random 5 percent sample was reviewed by hand; residual identifiers were found in 0.3 percent of sampled notes and removed.

found residual identifiers in 0.3 percent of the sampled notes

reference_answer: The model is HelixNet, trained on TerraNotes, whose notes come from 14 hospitals in Canada, Kenya and Chile.

question: HelixNet's accuracy drops on notes above a certain length. According to the survey, which model is most accurate on notes above that length?
reference_answer: HelixNet degrades above 16,000 tokens; on notes longer than 16,000 tokens the survey finds RMCT most accurate (F1 69.4).

evidence.quote: its accuracy drops sharply on notes longer than 16,000 tokens
On the subset of discharge summaries longer than 16,000 tokens, RMCT is the most accurate model, with an F1 of 69.4

question: What licence covers the data used to pre-train the model in the St. Aurelia pilot, and did the hospital's legal team consider its use allowed?
reference_answer: The model (HelixNet) was trained on TerraNotes, released under CC BY-NC 4.0 for research/non-commercial use; the legal team concluded internal, non-commercial use was permitted.

evidence.quote: released for research use only under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 licence (CC BY-NC 4.0)
the legal team concluded that internal, non-commercial use was permitted

question: Discuss the limitations of HelixNet.
reference_answer: English only; accuracy drops sharply on notes over 16,000 tokens (about 2 percent of summaries); likely reproduces training-corpus bias and was not audited by patient group; gives codes without explanations, so it should support rather than replace human coders.

evidence.quote: it was trained and evaluated only on English notes
its accuracy drops sharply on notes longer than 16,000 tokens

question: Compare HelixNet and WindowFormer on accuracy and memory use.
reference_answer: HelixNet is more accurate (71.8 vs 70.1 F1) and uses less memory (9.1 GB vs 14.3 GB); WindowFormer uses a larger 1,024-token window without global tokens.

evidence.quote: the reported micro-averaged F1 scores are 71.8 for HelixNet, 70.1 for WindowFormer and 70.9 for RMCT
Peak inference memory on a 9,000-token note was 9.1 GB for HelixNet, 14.3 GB for WindowFormer and 11.6 GB for RMCT

question: What risks did the St. Aurelia pilot reveal about assisted coding?
reference_answer: Worse performance on paediatric summaries (61 percent acceptance), suggestions for conditions ruled out later in the note, and coders over-relying on the top suggestion without reading the summary.

evidence.quote: The tool performed noticeably worse on paediatric discharge summaries
suggested codes for conditions that had been ruled out later in the same note
which the department considers a serious risk of over-reliance

question: What dataset was HelixNet trained on, and by how much did it reduce coding time in the hospital pilot?
reference_answer: TerraNotes; coding time fell by 31 percent (13 to 9 minutes).

evidence.quote: HelixNet was pre-trained and fine-tuned on the TerraNotes corpus
fell by 31 percent, from 13 minutes to 9 minutes

question: How many GPU hours did HelixNet training take, and what hardware ran it in the St. Aurelia pilot?
reference_answer: Training took 64 hours on eight A100 GPUs; the pilot ran on one on-premises server with two NVIDIA T4 GPUs.

evidence.quote: Training took 64 hours on eight A100 GPUs
a single on-premises server with two NVIDIA T4 GPUs

question: Summarize this document.
reference_answer: TerraNotes: 1.2 million English clinical notes (2015-2021) from 14 hospitals in Canada, Kenya and Chile, created by the Westbrook Health Data Consortium; 61 percent adult ICU, 4 percent paediatric; rule-based de-identification with a 5 percent manual review; hospital-assigned codes with about 7 percent error; patient-level 80/10/10 splits; CC BY-NC 4.0 research-only licence.

question: Give an overview of these documents.
reference_answer: HelixNet is a block-sparse clinical encoder that beats ClinBERT-L by 4.2 F1 using TerraNotes; TerraNotes is a 1.2M-note multi-site corpus with an ICU skew and CC BY-NC licence; a survey compares HelixNet, WindowFormer and RMCT, favouring HelixNet generally and RMCT for very long notes; a hospital pilot of HelixNet cut coding time by 31 percent but showed paediatric weakness and over-reliance risks.

question: What accuracy did HelixNet reach on chest X-ray image classification?
reference_answer: The documents do not report this: HelixNet is a text model and no image results are given.
